issues.title: Generator gradient formula lacks differentiability and domain hypotheses

diagnostic_evidence.quote: D(\mathcal{K}):=\{g\in \mathcal{F}(\Omega, \mathbb{C}): \hbox{limit in (\ref{koos}) exists for all } x\in \Omega \}

issues.failure_explanation: The old paper defines D(K) by existence of the forward orbit limit, then claims that topological-vector-space structure alone gives g'(x)·sigma'(0,x). For sigma(t,x)=x+t on R and g(x)=|x|, the forward generator limit exists at every x and equals 1 at x=0, while g'(0) does not exist. Thus the displayed right-hand side can be undefined for an observable in the stated pointwise domain.
issues.overall_effect: The gradient formula, and its later coordinate-wise repetition, is valid only on a suitable smooth generator core rather than on the entire pointwise generator domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the orbit-limit definition of the full generator domain, but qualify the gradient identity and its coordinate-wise repetition. If the orbit is right-differentiable at zero and g is differentiable at x, with the relevant continuity and bounded-difference-quotient conditions in the C_b setting, state K g(x)=Dg(x) sigma_t(0,x). For arbitrary g in D(K), assert only the orbit-limit formula.
issues.why_classification: The chain-rule inference needs a genuine missing premise, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the derivative appearing in the old display itself identifies the intended smooth-observable regime, and adding the standard differentiability qualification is a short local repair that leaves the general generator definition and the splitting method unchanged.

issues.title: Missing norm-continuity and generator-identification argument in bi-continuous splitting
issues.failure_explanation: The Lie-Trotter derivation uses norm derivatives although the preceding bi-continuous definitions initially supply weaker-topology continuity and generator limits with bounded norm difference quotients. The source does not supply the argument connecting these definitions to the norm generators used in the calculation. Its own stronger norm-density and contraction premises permit this connection; the allegation does not establish that additional substantive assumptions or a weaker convergence conclusion are necessary.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed norm-convergence argument has a missing continuity and generator-identification justification. This does not establish falsity of its norm-convergence conclusion and does not decide the separate convergence-rate assertions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use bounded norm difference quotients on the common domain, its norm density, and the contraction bounds to establish norm continuity of both semigroup factors. Establish the integrated semigroup identity to identify their bi-generators with their norm generators. Then apply the already stated strong Chernoff theorem using the existing domain and range density assumptions. Supply this connecting argument in the Lie-Trotter derivation without adding substantive hypotheses or weakening its conclusion to a tau-limit.
issues.why_classification: The complete continuity and generator-identification completion is contained mathematical work beyond the displayed calculation. Moderate is retained on the assessment that this completion is nontrivial; the rationale is its repair burden, not unavoidable new assumptions or weakening of the norm-convergence theorem. Merely observing that the strong Chernoff theorem is available does not supply the omitted connection.

issues.title: Lie-Trotter rate asserted without regularity assumptions

failure_location.quote:
The Lie-Trotter product formula has approximation order 1; that is, in general there exists a constant $M_{g,t}$ such that
     $$\|T(t)x - \left(V(\frac{t}{n})\right)^n x \| \le \frac{M_{x,t}}{n}.$$

issues.failure_explanation: The old prose claims an O(n^{-1}) error under the assumptions used for the preceding Chernoff convergence formula. What the old argument actually establishes there is derivative consistency and convergence. Its separate order discussion says that a global rate must come from control of V(h)-T(h), such as an O(h^2) local defect on the relevant orbit; no such control or domain regularity is imposed in the Lie-Trotter item. The claimed rate therefore exceeds the supplied support.
issues.overall_effect: The Lie-Trotter convergence formula may remain valid, but its advertised first-order global error bound is not established for every x covered by the convergence statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unconditional rate sentence by a conditional statement. For h=t/n, require a uniform local defect bound of the form ||(V(h)-T(h))T(kh)x|| <= C_{x,T} h^2 for kh<=T, established for example from explicit length-two word or commutator domain bounds. Together with the existing contraction stability, the telescoping identity then gives ||V(h)^n x-T(t)x|| <= C'_{x,T} t^2/n. Keep the bare Chernoff convergence statement separate from this rate claim.
issues.why_classification: Consistency and Chernoff convergence alone supply no first-order rate. Restricting the rate to a regularity class is a meaningful weakening of the advertised guarantee, so it is not minor, but the existing telescoping argument recovers the same O(n^{-1}) rate through a contained and standard argument. No global proof architecture is required.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Under the usual regularity assumptions for first-order splitting, the global error for fixed final time is of order $O(n^{-1})$, or equivalently $O(h)$ with $h=t/n$.

issues.title: Strang rate asserted without second-order regularity

failure_location.quote:
In general, the Strang product formula has approximation order 2; that is, in general there exists a constant $M_{g,t}$ such that
     $$\|T(t)x - \left(V(\frac{t}{n})\right)^n x \| \le \frac{M_{x,t}}{n^2}.$$

issues.failure_explanation: The old prose claims an O(n^{-2}) error under the assumptions supporting only the preceding product-formula convergence. The old paper's own order discussion shows that a global second-order rate requires an O(h^3) local defect and corresponding domain bounds. Neither the cancellation estimate nor those regularity assumptions are established in the Strang item, so the claimed rate is stronger than the supplied argument.
issues.overall_effect: The Strang product may still converge, but the second-order global bound is not established throughout the stated Banach-space regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unconditional rate sentence by a conditional statement. For h=t/n, require the Strang local defect estimate ||(V(h)-T(h))T(kh)x|| <= C_{x,T} h^3 uniformly for kh<=T, supported for example by explicit length-three word or commutator domain bounds and the symmetry cancellation. With the existing contraction stability, telescoping then yields ||V(h)^n x-T(t)x|| <= C'_{x,T} t^3/n^2.
issues.why_classification: The old assumptions establish convergence but not the second-order local cancellation or the regularity needed to control it. A comparable O(n^{-2}) result survives on a stated regularity class by a contained argument, but narrowing a central rate guarantee is more than a minor qualification. The repair does not require global reconstruction, so the issue is moderate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Under the usual regularity assumptions for second-order splitting, the global error for fixed final time is of order $O(n^{-2})$, or equivalently $O(h^2)$ with $h=t/n$.

issues.title: Complex higher-order factors lack sector-domain hypotheses

failure_location.quote: (or analytic contraction semigroups if the coefficients $\alpha_{j}$'s and $\beta_{j}$'s are complex)

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate is stated for products containing factors e^{alpha_j t K_i} and e^{beta_j t K_i}. The old hypotheses do not specify an analytic sector containing each complex ray, so they do not ensure that V_p(t) is defined for all coefficient choices admitted by the statement. An estimate for an undefined product cannot follow from the word-domain assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The higher-order estimate is not a well-defined assertion for all of its claimed complex-coefficient cases; the real-time case is unaffected by this particular root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the complex-coefficient branch, require for every coefficient c multiplying K_i that the analytic extension generated by K_i be defined on a sector containing the ray {c t: 0<=t<=T}. State the estimate only when every complex-time factor is thereby defined, while leaving the real-time branch unchanged.
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local compatibility condition needed to make the displayed product meaningful. It requires no new estimate or construction and does not change the order, rate, or real-coefficient result; cases outside the required sectors did not define a coherent product in the first place. Because a mathematical domain premise is missing, it is substantive but minor rather than a typo.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: If some coefficients are complex, assume that the relevant semigroups are analytic on sectors containing the rays determined by these coefficients.

issues.title: Higher-order estimate lacks a stability hypothesis
issues.failure_explanation: In the telescoping identity, each local defect is preceded by V_p(t/n)^{n-j-1}. The next displayed inequality drops this factor as if its norm were at most one. Algebraic order and the stated word-domain bounds do not provide that estimate. Without a uniform bound on these powers, the sum of local defects does not yield the claimed n^{-p} global estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The n^{-p} estimate in ha is unproved for compositions whose powers are not uniformly stable, even when every individual factor is defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the leading factor V_p(h)^(n-j-1) in the telescoping estimate and assume or prove uniform power stability C_T=sup{||V_p(h)^m||: h>=0 and mh<=T}<infinity. Bound each leading factor by C_T and combine this with the local O(h^(p+1)) defect estimate to recover the stated O(n^(-p)) global bound, with C_T absorbed into the constant.
issues.why_classification: Uniform stability is not supplied by algebraic order or the stated word-domain assumptions, and it is essential to the theorem's central global rate. Adding it produces a substantive but limited restriction. The same method and O(n^{-p}) conclusion then follow by a contained telescoping argument, so a comparable theorem survives without global reconstruction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Suppose that $V_p$ has algebraic order $p$ and is stable on $[0,T]$

issues.title: Missing one-half in the explicit fourth-order W composition
issues.failure_explanation: At either junction of two Strang factors, the adjacent K_2 half steps contribute a/2+(1-2a)/2=(1-a)/2. The old second junction instead uses (1-a), so the displayed W_[1] is not the composition defined by HO53 and even fails first-order coefficient consistency for K_2.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit seven-factor W_[1] formula does not represent the theorem's recursive fourth-order method as printed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the explicit formula for W_[1], replace the factor after exp((1-2a)t K_1) from exp((1-a)t K_2) to exp((1-a)t K_2/2). No other part of the recursive theorem needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The recursive definition HO53 uniquely forces both merged K_2 junctions to have coefficient (1-a)/2. The neighboring expansion and a direct multiplication of the three Strang factors determine the correction without any new inference or proof, making this a transcriptional missing factor.

issues.title: Frozen-coordinate maps need independent state-space invariance

diagnostic_evidence.quote: has unique, global, jointly continuous  solutions $\sigma(t,x) \in \Omega$ for all $x=(x_1,x_2)\in\Omega,$

issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims that the displayed coordinate formulas define Koopman operators and contractions on C_b(Omega). The old assumptions establish only that the full solution remains in Omega. For Omega equal to the unit circle and F(x,y)=(-y,x), the full rotation is global and Omega-invariant, but the first frozen update keeps y fixed and changes x linearly, leaving the circle for generic initial points. A function defined only on Omega then cannot be evaluated at the frozen state. Thus full-flow invariance does not support the claimed coordinate operators.
issues.overall_effect: The coordinate contractions and the two- and three-dimensional splitting algorithms can leave their declared state space and become undefined even though the original flow is valid on that space.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Before defining the coordinate Koopman operators or the associated two- and three-dimensional routines, assume explicitly that every frozen coordinate vector field generates a unique global, jointly continuous, Omega-invariant flow for the real substep times used. Define the coordinate operators and algorithms only under this independent frozen-flow hypothesis; do not infer it from invariance of the full flow.
issues.why_classification: Full-flow invariance does not imply frozen-coordinate invariance, and the omitted condition can make the operators and algorithms undefined on natural invariant state spaces. Adding the condition materially restricts the advertised input class, so the issue is not minor. The same coordinate method and conclusions remain recognizable on the restricted class through a local hypothesis change, so the issue is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Third-order state update discards the intermediate x value
issues.failure_explanation: After the second substep, the current x coordinate is x_{k+bar a}. The middle y substep does not reset x, so the following alpha-weighted x flow must start from that intermediate value. Starting it from x_k omits the preceding bar-alpha x update and therefore does not execute the composition in prop333.
issues.overall_effect: The printed five-step routine is not the stated third-order splitting map, so its claimed third-order update and error behavior do not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the fourth substep, start the alpha-weighted x-flow from the intermediate x value produced in the second substep, rather than from x_k; equivalently, use x_{k+bar a} as the final argument of that sigma call.
issues.why_classification: The preceding substep explicitly computes the current x value, and the intervening y update does not alter it. The stated five-factor composition therefore uniquely fixes the corrected argument. This is a copied stage-index error requiring no new construction or analysis.

issues.title: Complex-coefficient routine lacks a complex-time frozen-flow contract
issues.failure_explanation: The old flow contract is for t in [0,infinity) and states in a real Omega, while the third-order routine evaluates gamma and sigma at times involving the nonreal coefficient a and its conjugate. Neither complex-time maps nor a complex extension of the intermediate state domain is supplied, so the procedure is undefined for a general real frozen flow.
issues.overall_effect: The complex third-order algorithms cannot be applied throughout the advertised class of real globally solvable ODEs; their order claim is meaningful only for systems with an appropriate complex extension.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the complex-coefficient routine to systems for which the frozen maps have compatible complex-time extensions on a complexified state domain containing every coefficient time and every intermediate state generated by the composition. State that the third-order routine and its order claim are unavailable under the merely real flow contract unless this additional contract is verified.
issues.why_classification: The old real-time flow assumptions do not define any of the nonreal stages, and imposing a compatible complex extension excludes a natural and substantial part of the advertised real-ODE input class. The restriction is nevertheless local and leaves the same third-order composition recognizable for systems satisfying it, so the issue has a complete moderate repair rather than requiring removal or global reconstruction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: This formula assumes that the frozen maps $\sigma_y(s,x)$ and $\gamma_x(s,y)$ are available for the complex time parameters appearing above.

issues.title: Three-dimensional Strang update violates the frozen z-flow interface
issues.failure_explanation: The declared frozen z-flow has signature tau_{x,y}(s,z). The first old z half-step instead supplies y_k and z_k as its frozen coordinates. The final half-step supplies y_{k+1} and the not-yet-defined z_{k+1}. These calls are incompatible with the declared map and cannot implement the symmetric frozen-coordinate sequence.
issues.overall_effect: The printed three-dimensional Strang routine is not executable as written and does not define the state map represented by SPH.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the declared frozen z-flow interface in both z half-steps: set z_{k+1/2}=tau_{x_k,y_k}(h/2,z_k) and z_{k+1}=tau_{x_{k+1},y_{k+1}}(h/2,z_{k+1/2}), where h=t/n.
issues.why_classification: The signature tau_{x,y}(s,z) and the symmetric z-y-x-y-z sequence uniquely determine both corrected calls. The old first call permutes its frozen arguments and the last uses an undefined output as an input; both are immediately identifiable interface-transcription errors, with no proof or algorithmic design choice required.
